I added the `bulk-refunds` flag and gated `refund()` behind it. I haven't run any tests or imported the module.

- **`flags.toml`**: declared `bulk-refunds = false`. Per the project's flag convention, a flag has to be declared there before code reads it. Otherwise `is_on()` quietly returns `False`.
- **`src/billing/refunds.py`**: `refund()` now checks `is_on("bulk-refunds")` from `src/flags.py` first. If the flag is off, it raises `RuntimeError("refunds are disabled: bulk-refunds flag is off")`.

You didn't say what `refund()` should do when the flag is off, so I made it raise. If you'd rather it return `None` or fall back to some other behavior, that's a one-line change.

Nothing else in the repo calls `refund()` today, so no other code is affected. With the default `false`, refunds stay off until you flip the flag.
